question: True or false: nitrous oxide, the laughing gas used by dentists, can explode with no fuel present?
answer: True. Nitrous oxide breaks down into nitrogen and oxygen, giving off heat, so a hot spot can set off a runaway decomposition inside the tank itself. In 2007 a nitrous flow test at Scaled Composites in Mojave, with no fuel present, exploded and killed three workers.
move: Check whether a harmless ingredient can react with itself.
trap: Treating an oxidiser as inert until a fuel is added.
reference: Karabeyoglu, Dyer, Stevens & Cantwell, Modeling of N2O Decomposition Events, AIAA 2008-4933, 44th Joint Propulsion Conference, 2008
